title: Honorary sheriff and deputy commissions from Odessa and beyond
summary: Fulcher has the Odessa sheriff swear in Leeman and others as honorary deputies, with Stetsons and silver buckles, and Leeman collects commissions in several counties given his love of law enforcement.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: And of course, Flip Phillips was another of his loves, which I have mentioned. And he knew my love for guns and my interest in hunting, and also on becoming a sheriff -- my father was up to high sheriff in Cumberland County, Portland, Maine when he died -- he died just before attaining the office of high sheriff. I have his badges and also badges and the history of my grandmother's brother, Sam Taylor -- a well known policeman and sheriff in Portland, Maine in the late 1890's and early 1900's. I was always obgessed with police work and law and order -- even if I was for a period of my life a crazy SB, as we would say with tongue in cheek.
I was also deeply into studies of the Old West and

how it was won, and Jim Fulcher knew all these things, and along the way, one of the parties we did, he had the sheriff of Odessa swear me in as an honorary sheriff in front of an audience, during a concert.

And he had a little gold badge for us, and there were two or three guys -- I think Yank Lawson and Cutty Cutshall, and Bud Freeman, I believe, and the guys that were in on that particular party -- and we used to wear those little badges in case we got stopped in Odessa, because we had the swagger, and we are now honorary deputies.

And he presented the whole group at that particular time, with silver western buckels and everybody got a western rancher's dress Stetson hat. I think that particular party we were on, about 15 people -- this little party was going at the time, and I still have the Stetson, and I've put that thing under hot water and I've reshaped it, and around the crown I've got some Mexican silver doodads -- and I still wear it everyplace. All over the world, in fact. To Europe and Switzerland and so forth. I don't know whether the other guys have theirs yet.

And the next few years -- to continue in this vein -- Fulcher arranged for the then mayor, Jim Reese, in 1972, also a jazz fan at our parties, and he had reached -- swear me in and made me an official honorary citizen of Odessa, Texas. That's hanging here on the wall. And he did that so

I could be - and did become eventually as a citizen, I could legitimately recieve a regular commission in the sheriff's department of Ector County, Texas - and he set that up for me -- one of the bright happy lights in my life.

The sheriff then was Elwood Hill, and I got my new badge in 1977 and my ID -- no, I got the regular commission from Sheriff Hill and later on, the new sheriff, that lasted two or three years, Sheriff Faught -- and my new badge in '77 and ID is under Sheriff Faught. Since then, I have received my sheriff's commission.

I'm a little confused here, because I don't know what I gave -- said it as it is, I got a regular commission in the sheriff's department under Elwood Hill, and then as the sheriff's changed, the new badge, the one that I carry with me now, is from Elwood Faught, and of course, the sheriffs change after you have your new ID card.

I also carry and hold a full commission on Jefferson County, Arkansas sheriff's department, and I carry that badge. I ws saying before that I have a commission -- and it's a full commission, but it's all over now because that sheriff is gone -- Bernalillo County in the state of New Mexico, I got a full commission in Jefferson County, as I just said, and I am an honorary citizen of Pine Bluff, Arkansas -- to make that commission binding, and one last aside, and I will finish with the Odessa parties.
